record.context_brief: Commuting operator for the finite-n GUE kernel
record.original_question: Let Kn be the restriction to L^2([s,+infinity)) of the projection onto the first n probabilistic Hermite functions, with kernel Kn(x, y) = sum_{k=0}^{n-1} phi_k(x) phi_k(y). Can one find a differential operator commuting with Kn on L^2([s,+infinity)), and what are its eigenvectors? The operator need not be second order, but it should converge in a suitable rescaled sense to LTW,s.

evidence.quote: The GUE kernel operator is the restriction to L^2([s, +infinity)) of the projection on the first n vectors of L^2(R) with the (probabilistic) Hermite functions, i.e. Kn(x, y) := sum_{k=0}^{n-1} phi_k(x) phi_k(y).

Question 2. Can one find a commuting differential operator to Kn acting on L^2([s, +infinity)) ? What are its eigenvectors ? Such an operator is not necessarily of the second order, but it should converge in some sense to LTW,s when suitably rescaled.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\{\phi_k\}_{k\geq 0}$ denote the probabilistic Hermite functions on $\mathbb{R}$, i.e. the $L^2(\mathbb{R})$-orthonormal eigenfunctions of the harmonic oscillator obtained by multiplying the (probabilistic) Hermite polynomials by the Gaussian weight $(2\pi)^{-1/4} e^{-x^2/4}$. For each integer $n\geq 1$ and each $s\in\mathbb{R}$, let $K_n$ be the integral operator on $L^2([s,+\infty))$ with kernel
$$K_n(x,y)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\phi_k(x)\phi_k(y),\qquad x,y\in[s,+\infty),$$
that is, the restriction to $L^2([s,+\infty))$ of the orthogonal projection in $L^2(\mathbb{R})$ onto the span of $\phi_0,\dots,\phi_{n-1}$. Recall further the Tracy–Widom differential operator
$$L_{TW,s}f(x)=-\frac{d^2 f}{dx^2}(x)+(x-s)f(x),\qquad x\geq 0,$$
acting on $L^2([0,+\infty))$ with the Dirichlet boundary condition $f(0)=0$, which is known to commute with the Airy kernel integral operator on $L^2([s,+\infty))$ in the edge-scaling limit.

Problem. Exhibit a (not necessarily second-order) linear differential operator $\mathcal{D}_{n,s}$ acting on a suitable dense subspace of $L^2([s,+\infty))$ such that $\mathcal{D}_{n,s}$ commutes with $K_n$ on $L^2([s,+\infty))$, and describe its eigenfunctions. The operator $\mathcal{D}_{n,s}$ should, under an appropriate rescaling $x\mapsto \sqrt{4n}+x/(2\, n^{1/6})$ near the soft edge, converge in a suitable sense to $L_{TW,s}$ as $n\to\infty$.
artifact.category_tag: commuting differential operators for random-matrix kernels
artifact.status_search_result: For symmetric intervals $[-t,t]$, Tracy–Widom and others have exhibited second-order differential operators commuting with the finite-$n$ Hermite (GUE) kernel; recent work (e.g. Grünbaum and collaborators) constructs algebras of commuting differential operators for Airy-type kernels. However, for the one-sided restriction to $[s,+\infty)$ of the finite-$n$ Hermite projection, an explicit commuting differential operator that rescales to the Tracy–Widom operator $L_{TW,s}$ at the soft edge does not appear in the standard literature, and the question seems to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Level-spacing distributions and the Airy kernel
status_evidence.snippet: Tracy and Widom exhibit a second-order differential operator commuting with the Airy kernel integral operator on (s, infinity); analogous commuting operators are known for the sine and Hermite (symmetric interval) kernels.
status_evidence.claim: Commuting differential operators are known for the Airy kernel and for the finite-n Hermite kernel on symmetric intervals.

status_evidence.title: Algebras of Commuting Differential Operators for Kernels of Airy Type
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of algebras of commuting differential operators for kernels of Airy type, extending Tracy–Widom-type results.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work constructs commuting differential operators for Airy-type kernels, but does not give an explicit one for the finite-n GUE kernel restricted to a half-line [s,infty).

status_evidence.title: Fredholm determinants, differential equations and matrix models
status_evidence.snippet: Tracy–Widom framework for finite-n matrix kernels using commuting differential operators on symmetric intervals.
status_evidence.claim: The standard finite-n GUE commuting operator construction is for symmetric intervals, not for half-lines [s,infty).
